title: Kaplan Fibres

positions.as_written: Expect them to be divided in any approach that elevates the iliotibial band from the distal femur, and record that they were.
Consider them when a knee has rotational laxity after a technically sound cruciate reconstruction, since nothing in the standard examination tests them directly.
Identify the supracondylar ridge as the landmark for their femoral attachment, not the epicondyle.
Preserve them where an approach allows, because their contribution is not reproduced by anything else.
Treat rotational restraint on the lateral side as the sum of these fibres, the capsulo-osseous layer and the anterolateral ligament, rather than attributing it to one structure.
Consider a lateral extra-articular procedure in a knee with a high grade pivot shift, and understand it as reproducing this attachment rather than adding a new structure.
Plan the femoral fixation from the supracondylar ridge and proximal to the collateral ligament, so the two constructs do not compete for bone.
Avoid over-tensioning a construct in this position.
